pr_title: fix: Semi-join and multiple keys outer-join did not respect POLARS_MAX_THREADS
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/14535

This happens because a `ParallelIterator` is constructed inside of `POOL.install` but this iterator is collected outside of the `POOL` context. I.e.:

```rust
POOL.install(|| { x.par_iter().map(..) }).collect() // this runs outside the pool
POOL.install(|| { x.par_iter().map(..).collect() }) // this runs inside the pool
```

This was hard to spot at first because we see `POOL.install` next to `par_iter` and are led to believe it is used properly, but in fact the key requirement was to ensure the iteration (usually `.collect()`) was being done inside of `POOL.install`.

I also fixed some other places aside from semi-join that did this (but restricted to `crates/polars-ops/src/frame/join/`)

Not sure how to add tests for this, but here's a reproducible script:
```python
def f(k, how):
    import psutil
    import os

    os.environ["POLARS_MAX_THREADS"] = "1"
    import polars as pl

    print("Num threads: {}".format(psutil.Process().num_threads()))
    print(f"{pl.thread_pool_size()=}")

    df1 = pl.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": [4, 5, 6]})
    df2 = pl.DataFrame({"a": [1, 4, 5], "c": [4, 5, 6]}).with_columns(b="c")

    df1.join(df2.select(k), on=k, how=how)
    print(
        f"finish {how}-join ({'multiple keys' if len(k) > 1 else 'single key'}), {k=}"
    )
    print("Num threads: {}".format(psutil.Process().num_threads()))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from multiprocessing import get_context

    for k in (("a",), ("a", "b")):
        for how in ("inner", "left", "outer", "semi", "anti"):
            # Run every combination in a new process
            with get_context("spawn").Pool(1) as p:
                p.starmap(f, [(k, how)])

```
This is a screenshot showing the output diff before/after (my machine has 8 threads):
![image](https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/assets/93244543/f92c8d31-a192-4172-b341-0007e4db697c)

issue_context.title: Polars 'POLARS_MAX_THREADS' doesn't work when doing a Semi join
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import os

os.environ['POLARS_MAX_THREADS'] = '1'

import psutil
print('Num threads before: {}'.format(psutil.Process().num_threads()))

import polars as pl

print(pl.thread_pool_size())
print('Num threads before: {}'.format(psutil.Process().num_threads()))

df1 = pl.DataFrame({'a': [1,2,3],
                   'b': [4,5,6]})
df2 = pl.DataFrame({'a': [1,4,5],
                   'c': [4,5,6]})
df1 = df1.join(df2, on="a")

print(pl.thread_pool_size())
print('Num threads before: {}'.format(psutil.Process().num_threads()))

df1 = df1.join(df2, on="a", how="semi")

print(pl.thread_pool_size())
print('Num threads before: {}'.format(psutil.Process().num_threads()))
```


### Log output

```shell
Num threads before: 12
1
Num threads before: 13
1
Num threads before: 13
1
Num threads before: 29
```


### Issue description

When doing a semi join between two Polars Dataframes the num of threads appear to jump above what is set when using POLARS_MAX_THREADS. On the server that I was running this example it had 16cpus and the increase was 16 threads. When running on a server with 32cpus the increase from the semi join was also 32 in that case.
It appears to be a similar issue to https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/10847 and I have made a similar example as above.

### Expected behavior

Num threads shouldn't increase for a semi join.
